- If sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.7) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slope or cap upward momentum.
- If sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -0.3) in recent days, model tends to underestimate prices; increase forecast baseline or add downward bias.
- Model consistently overestimates after sharp upward spikes in sentiment (e.g., sentiment = 1.0 followed by forecast rise); apply lagged correction or dampen momentum.
- Forecast often fails to capture mean reversion after prolonged upward trends; add a decay factor or adjust for recent volatility.
- For 30-day horizon, model frequently overpredicts early in the window when sentiment is neutral or mildly positive; reduce initial forecast values.
- If sentiment history shows repeated “recovery” patterns (e.g., negative → positive), model tends to overshoot; apply smoothing or reduce forecast amplitude.
- When sentiment is high and price is rising, model often fails to account for regulatory or policy-induced corrections; add a downward adjustment buffer.
